mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about gases reflects a common misconception?

options.A: Gases have a fixed shape and fixed volume.
options.B: Gases expand to fill the shape of any container they occupy.
options.C: Gases are highly compressible because their particles are far apart.
options.D: Gases exert pressure on the walls of their container due to particle collisions.

mcqs.answer: Gases have a fixed shape and fixed volume.
mcqs.explanation: Option B, C and D correctly describe gases: they have no fixed shape, they expand to fill any container, they are compressible because particles are far apart, and they exert pressure due to collisions. Option A is a misconception; gases do NOT have a fixed shape or volume. Hence A is the incorrect statement being asked for.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare shape and volume of different states
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the shape and volume of solids, liquids and gases?

options.A: Solids have a fixed shape and volume; liquids have a fixed shape but variable volume; gases have variable shape and volume.
options.B: Solids have a fixed shape and volume; liquids have no fixed shape but a fixed volume; gases have no fixed shape and no fixed volume.
options.C: Solids have no fixed shape but a fixed volume; liquids have a fixed shape and volume; gases have a fixed shape and no volume.
options.D: All three states have a fixed shape and a fixed volume.

mcqs.answer: Solids have a fixed shape and volume; liquids have no fixed shape but a fixed volume; gases have no fixed shape and no fixed volume.
mcqs.explanation: Solids retain both shape and volume. Liquids take the shape of their container but keep a constant volume. Gases take both the shape and the volume of the container. Option B states exactly this. Options A, C and D contain incorrect combinations of shape and volume for the states.

mcqs.question: Which set correctly matches the particle arrangement with a characteristic property for each state of matter?

options.A: Solids: particles far apart, high compressibility; Liquids: particles close, definite shape; Gases: particles tightly packed, low kinetic energy.
options.B: Solids: particles tightly packed, definite shape; Liquids: particles close but free to move, definite volume; Gases: particles far apart, highly compressible.
options.C: Solids: particles close but free to move, variable volume; Liquids: particles far apart, fixed shape; Gases: particles tightly packed, fixed volume.
options.D: Solids: particles arranged in layers, high diffusion; Liquids: particles in random motion, low diffusion; Gases: particles in a lattice, high diffusion.

mcqs.answer: Solids: particles tightly packed, definite shape; Liquids: particles close but free to move, definite volume; Gases: particles far apart, highly compressible.
mcqs.explanation: In solids, particles are tightly packed in fixed positions giving a definite shape and volume. In liquids, particles are close together but can slide past each other, giving a definite volume but no fixed shape. In gases, particles are far apart, move freely, and the gas is highly compressible. Option B captures these facts. Options A, C and D contain incorrect descriptions of particle spacing or resulting properties.

mcqs.question: Why are gases much more compressible than liquids?

options.A: Gas particles are far apart, so reducing the volume brings them closer with little resistance.
options.B: Gas particles are tightly packed, so they can be squeezed easily.
options.C: Liquid particles are far apart, making liquids more compressible than gases.
options.D: Gas particles have strong attractive forces that allow them to be compressed easily.

mcqs.answer: Gas particles are far apart, so reducing the volume brings them closer with little resistance.
mcqs.explanation: Compressibility depends on the amount of empty space between particles. In gases the particles are far apart, so the volume can be decreased considerably before particles start to collide strongly. Liquids have particles much closer together, leaving little space to reduce, so they are barely compressible. Options B, C and D describe incorrect reasons for compressibility.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes a solid?

options.A: It has a definite shape and volume; its particles vibrate about fixed positions.
options.B: It has no definite shape but a definite volume; its particles move freely.
options.C: It has no definite shape and no definite volume; its particles are far apart.
options.D: It has a definite shape but no definite volume; its particles are tightly packed.

mcqs.answer: It has a definite shape and volume; its particles vibrate about fixed positions.
mcqs.explanation: Solids retain both a fixed shape and a fixed volume because their particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate in place. Options B and C describe liquids and gases respectively, while D mixes attributes incorrectly.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a liquid?

options.A: It has a definite shape and volume; its particles vibrate in fixed positions.
options.B: It has no definite shape but a definite volume; its particles are close together and can slide past each other.
options.C: It has no definite shape and no definite volume; its particles are far apart and move independently.
options.D: It has a definite shape but no definite volume; its particles are tightly packed.

mcqs.answer: It has no definite shape but a definite volume; its particles are close together and can slide past each other.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids take the shape of their container (no fixed shape) but keep a constant volume. Their particles are close together, allowing them to flow past one another. Option A describes solids, C describes gases, and D mixes properties incorrectly.

mcqs.question: Which description best distinguishes gases from solids and liquids?

options.A: Gases have a definite shape and volume; particles vibrate in fixed positions.
options.B: Gases have no definite shape but a definite volume; particles are close together.
options.C: Gases have no definite shape and no definite volume; particles are far apart and move freely.
options.D: Gases have a definite shape but no volume; particles are tightly packed.

mcqs.answer: Gases have no definite shape and no definite volume; particles are far apart and move freely.
mcqs.explanation: Gases expand to fill any container, showing neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume. Their particles are widely spaced and move independently. Options A and D incorrectly assign solid-like properties, while B incorrectly gives gases a fixed volume.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare shape and volume of different states
mcqs.question: A sealed container holds water at the bottom and air above it. Which statement about the shape and volume of the water and the air inside the container is correct?

options.A: Water has a fixed shape and volume; air takes the shape of the container and its volume changes with pressure.
options.B: Water takes the shape of the container; air has a fixed shape and volume.
options.C: Both water and air have fixed shape and volume.
options.D: Both water and air take the shape of the container but have fixed volume.

mcqs.answer: Water has a fixed shape and volume; air takes the shape of the container and its volume changes with pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Liquid water retains its volume but conforms to the shape of the container, while the gas (air) expands to fill any remaining space, taking the container's shape and being compressible, so its volume can change with pressure. Options B, C and D misrepresent the behavior of liquids and gases.
